version.changelog:
- Added CLI support for a16z Speedrun and South Park Commons, alongside YC Startup School.
- New commands for submitting, previewing, and managing Speedrun and SPC applications directly from the terminal.
- Expanded quick reference and command documentation to cover multiple workflows and automation options.
- Added browser automation for SPC applications and enhanced browser profile selection for YC flows.
- Improved documentation, including detailed usage examples and explanations for each command.

llm.summary: The package and runtime instructions are consistent with a CLI that automates Startup School, a16z Speedrun, and SPC workflows — it reads browser cookies and uses Playwright and creates a Claude/skill symlink during install, which are sensitive but explainable by the stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (YC Startup School, Speedrun, SPC) matches the code and dependencies: cookie extraction for Startup School, Playwright for Airtable/SPC automation, and upload/HTTP clients for Speedrun. Requiring a yc binary (the package installs the 'yc' CLI) and including playwright/@steipete/sweet-cookie are proportionate to the stated features.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and SKILL.md direct the agent to install the npm package and run commands that read browser cookies (Chrome/macOS) and optionally run headless Playwright to fill/submit Airtable forms. Those actions are sensitive (reading Chrome cookies, interacting with macOS Keychain) but are explicitly required by the skill's functionality and are limited to the claimed services (startupschool.org, airtable.com, speedrun endpoints). There is no instruction to collect unrelated system files or to exfiltrate data to unexpected endpoints in the provided materials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is via npm (@lucasygu/yc-cli) — a standard, traceable registry source. Playwright will pull browser binaries as expected. The postinstall script creates a symlink in ~/.claude/skills/yc-cli to integrate with Claude Code and also patches files inside node_modules/@steipete/sweet-cookie to work around bugs; modifying dependency files during postinstall is unusual but plausible as a compatibility fix. This behavior increases attack-surface (writes to disk and edits installed package files) and is worth reviewing before install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, which is appropriate. However, it requires access to browser cookies and (on macOS) keychain prompts to read/decrypt Chrome cookies — highly sensitive local credentials. That access is justified by the need to authenticate to startupschool.org but is a meaningful privacy/security consideration the user must accept.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced global inclusion). The postinstall creates a persistent symlink under ~/.claude/skills so the CLI is automatically available as a Claude Code/OpenClaw skill — this is a deliberate persistent integration but limited to the agent skill directory and reversible by uninstall. The package does not request system-wide privileges beyond normal filesystem writes and the ability to patch dependency files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to do what it says, but it performs several sensitive actions that you should consciously accept before installing: it reads Chrome session cookies (and thus triggers macOS Keychain prompts) to authenticate to startupschool.org; it uses Playwright which will download and run headless Chromium; and its postinstall script creates a symlink in ~/.claude/skills and patches files inside node_modules to workaround bugs. Before installing: (1) inspect the package source (https://github.com/lucasygu/yc-cli) and confirm you trust the author; (2) review scripts/postinstall.js to ensure you are comfortable with the symlink and patch behavior; (3) consider installing with scripts disabled (npm install --ignore-scripts) and manually creating the ~/.claude/skills symlink if you want manual control; (4) do not click “Always Allow” on Keychain prompts unless you trust the package and machine; (5) if you need extra safety, run installation and initial use in an isolated account or VM to limit access to your primary browser profile and keychain.
